title: Confidence-driven KV cache quantization harness and progressive rollout plan
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Evaluate a confidence-driven, runtime-gated approach for applying INT8/FP8 quantization to the KV cache to reduce token-serving cost while bounding accuracy regressions. This ticket scopes an experiment harness, metric suite, and staged rollout playbook that avoids all-or-nothing switches and uses a quality budget curve to control tail latency and delta-quality trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: A/B harness that can run shadow traffic against float32, INT8, and FP8 KV variants with identical request routing
Metric suite implemented: delta-token-match, golden-token-drift, logprob-delta, hallucination-rate, and latency p50/p90/p99
Confidence gating policy implemented in runtime to fallback on per-request basis when quality budget would be exceeded
Safety rollback triggers and monitoring dashboards wired into Console for per-customer traffic
Documented progressive rollout plan with smoke tests and abort thresholds
experiment_plan: Phase 0 - Harness: create kv_shadow harness that mirrors production routing for 7 days and records token-level outputs for a sample of traffic (path: infra/kv_shadow/2026-02)

Phase 1 - Offline profiling: run stochastic calibration sweeps to generate per-layer FP8/INT8 profiles across representative workloads (chat, completions, long-context retrieval) and store profiles in /artifacts/quant_profiles/2026-02
Phase 2 - Shadow eval: replay 100k requests through quantized KV runtime (int8, fp8-e4m3, fp8-e5m2 hybrid) in shadow mode and compute delta-token-match and logprob-delta vs float baseline

Phase 3 - Confidence model: train lightweight confidence estimator on prefix statistics (logprob variance, attention norm deltas, token-type) to decide per-request quant gating with an explicit quality budget parameter
Phase 4 - Canary: enable confidence-gated INT8 on 0.5% of production traffic for low-risk orgs with strict real-time monitoring and auto-abort on metric drift
Phase 5 - Progressive ramp: ramp to 5%, 25%, then 100% for dedicated pools if success criteria met; for hosted, keep conservative caps and provide opt-in customer controls
measurement_definition: delta-token-match: fraction of tokens where generated token != baseline top-1 token (lower is better)
golden-token-drift: mean edit-distance between generated sequences and oracle reference prompt outputs
logprob-delta: mean token log probability difference compared to float baseline
hallucination-rate: fraction of responses that fail task-specific factual checks (measured per prompt set)
latency: p50/p90/p99 token generation latency, and cold-start tail for KV miss
cost-per-token: GPU time-normalized token cost estimate for each quant variant
results_summary: Initial offline profiling found that a hybrid FP8(INT8 for low-variance heads) profile reduced per-token GPU compute by ~28% vs float baseline with mean logprob-delta of 0.03 and delta-token-match 0.9% on retrieval-augmented prompts. Shadow replay (100k requests) showed p90 latency improvement of 12ms for INT8 paths but a 0.4% increase in hallucination-rate on question-answer prompts. The confidence estimator reduced observed delta-token-match to 0.35% at the cost of limiting quantized execution to 63% of requests, yielding ~17% net cost savings. Detailed traces and artifacts: https://go.redwood/kv-quant/2026-03-shadow-results and PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/5823
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Rare long-context prompts produce compounding logprob drift -> Mitigation: enforce conservative gating for sequences > 2048 tokens and shadow validate long-context buckets
Risk: Per-customer model/finetune sensitivity -> Mitigation: add per-customer baseline extrapolation and allow customer opt-out flags in Console
Risk: Quant calibration profile drift over time (distributional shift) -> Mitigation: daily lightweight re-calibration job and drift detector that marks profiles stale
Risk: Increased p99 tail under certain batch mixes -> Mitigation: introduce latency-aware scheduling and limit quantized batches under tight SLOs
rollout_playbook: Pre-roll: run 7-day shadow and verify that logprob-delta < 0.05 AND hallucination-rate delta < 0.25% for target workload
Canary steps: enable 0.5% with circuit-breaker metrics (logprob-delta, delta-token-match, p99 latency); auto-abort on >2x expected delta or user-visible regressions
Operator checks: smoke-test set (10 prompts per app pattern) and manual sign-off by SRE and ML quality lead
Post-roll: schedule 24h intensive monitoring with high-frequency sampling and daily calibration job for first week
Undo: immediate revert to float KV and blacklist offending model versions/customers
comments: 2026-02-22 Miguel Alvarez: Hooked up shadow harness to traffic mirror and started ingesting token-level traces. Sample rate set to 0.1% to limit storage. Observed initial memory footprint drop on NVIDIA H100 by ~22% for INT8 path.

2026-02-27 Priya Desai (ML): Ran stochastic calibration sweeps; FP8 e4m3 profiles are surprisingly robust on chat workloads but fragile on open-domain QA. Adding per-layer variance thresholding to selection heuristics.
2026-03-03 SRE On-call (Jason Lee): Noted transient p99 spikes during mixed workloads when quantized and float batches co-schedule. Implementing separate worker pool affinity for quantized jobs.
2026-03-08 Miguel Alvarez: Confidence estimator prototype decreased delta-token-match in shadow runs. Need product sign-off on acceptable hallucination uplift before canary.

2026-03-10 Product review (Becky Chan): Approved canary for low-risk internal orgs with the following conditions: 24h smoke window, revert playbook, and customer opt-out in Console. Assigned rollout owner to Solutions Eng.
